solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Managing course

definitions.meaning: in building, the top layer of a wall, a course of brick or stone that caps it

explanation.definitionFit: One sense is getting by under pressure; the other is the capping layer of masonry along a wall's top.

clue.text: Why theatre can't perform Robinson Crusoe?

definitions.meaning: a show cannot go on when the actors are all absent, read as two words
the shipwrecked sailor of Defoe's novel, marooned on an island

explanation.walkthrough: Split, the answer says the actors are away; whole, it is someone marooned.
explanation.definitionFit: Crusoe is literature's most famous shipwrecked sailor, stranded alone on an island.

clue.text: I hope to cop off, having right image-maker!

indicators.note: off means gone wrong or out of order, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone hopes to pull a police officer, having the right image.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cop off' is British slang for getting off with someone romantically; 'off' alone signals the rearrangement.
explanation.definitionFit: A photocopier makes images of documents, so it is literally a maker of copies.

clue.text: Zip over European river

indicators.note: in a down clue, over means placed on top of what follows

parts.note: zip is slang for nothing, nil

explanation.surface: Speeding across a river in Europe.
explanation.definitionFit: The Nile is the great river of north-east Africa, often called the world's longest.

clue.text: Praise champion keeping company with youth

indicators.note: keeping means holding something within, so the word for champion holds the other pieces

parts.note: an ace is a champion or expert
a lad is a youth

explanation.surface: A sports champion is praised while spending time with a young person.
explanation.definitionFit: An accolade is an award or expression of praise, so the noun matches the noun.

clue.text: The old bores turned up drunk

indicators.note: bores means drills into, so the old word for the goes inside

parts.note: a cocked hat or ear is one turned up
ye is the archaic form of the

explanation.surface: The old tedious people arrived plastered.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bores' looks like dull people; it is the verb, drilling into. 'turned up' looks like arrived.
explanation.definitionFit: Cockeyed is informal slang for intoxicated, besides crooked.

clue.text: Who so raved about eclipse?

indicators.note: about means round and about, so these letters are scrambled

explanation.surface: A question about who got so excited over an eclipse.
explanation.definitionFit: To overshadow is to outshine or put in the shade, the figurative sense of eclipse.

clue.text: Indeed organ can be heard

indicators.note: can be heard says the word for the organ is spoken, giving a word that sounds the same

parts.note: the eye is the organ of sight

explanation.surface: A church organ can indeed be heard.
explanation.walkthrough: 'organ' suggests a church instrument; it is the body part.
explanation.definitionFit: Aye is a dialect or archaic yes, an affirmation like indeed.

clue.text: Consider ending of Close Encounters revolutionary

indicators.note: ending of points to the final letter of the word close
revolutionary means turning round, so the word for encounters is written backwards

parts.note: meets means encounters

explanation.surface: Think about the finale of the film Close Encounters as groundbreaking.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Close Encounters' reads as the film title; 'revolutionary' reverses MEETS to STEEM.
explanation.definitionFit: To esteem can mean to regard or deem, a formal sense of consider.

clue.text: Supporting Sunderland, say? That's apt

parts.note: pro means in favour of, supporting
Sunderland is a city in North East England, abbreviated NE

explanation.surface: Backing Sunderland football club, a fitting thing to do.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Sunderland' suggests the football club; it stands for its region, the North East of England.
explanation.definitionFit: Prone means inclined or liable, as in 'apt to' do something.

clue.text: One in senior nursing post is type who ruins things

indicators.note: the clue word that signals this step
to nurse is to hold close, so the abbreviation for senior holds the post, which itself holds the numeral

parts.note: a pole is a post
one is the Roman numeral I

explanation.surface: A troublemaker has crept into a senior care post and wrecks everything.
explanation.walkthrough: 'nursing' reads as caring for patients; here it means holding, the outer of two containers, with 'in' as the inner one.
explanation.definitionFit: A spoiler is someone who wrecks things for others, as a spoilsport does.

clue.text: Caught by copper, maybe not the first that's lenient

parts.note: C is the cricket abbreviation for caught

indicators.note: not the first says the opening letter of the word for copper is dropped

parts.note: copper is an example of a chemical element

explanation.surface: Arrested by a police officer, perhaps not for the first offence, so the treatment is mild.
explanation.walkthrough: 'copper' looks like a policeman doing the catching; here it is the metal, an element.
explanation.definitionFit: Clement is a formal synonym for merciful or mild, as a judge might be.

clue.text: A kiss acceptable? Bit of nerve required

parts.note: X is the cross that stands for a kiss at the end of a letter
on, as in 'that's not on', means acceptable

explanation.surface: Someone wonders whether a kiss is allowed, and needs a little courage to try.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bit of nerve' reads as boldness but means part of a nerve cell.
explanation.definitionFit: An axon is the long fibre of a nerve cell, literally a piece of a nerve.

clue.text: After universal mobile ban, selfie is not possible

indicators.note: after places the jumbled letters behind the letter for universal

parts.note: U is the film-rating abbreviation for universal

indicators.note: mobile means moving about, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Once phones are banned everywhere, taking a selfie becomes impossible.
explanation.walkthrough: 'mobile' looks like the phone being banned; it signals that BAN and SELFIE are rearranged.
explanation.definitionFit: Unfeasible means impracticable, something that cannot be done.

clue.text: Teeth I'd lost in raid? That's come to nothing

indicators.note: in places the mixed letters inside the word for raid

parts.note: a bust is a police raid

indicators.note: lost means gone astray, so these letters are mixed up

explanation.surface: Someone lost teeth in a police raid, and their plans came to nothing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'lost' rearranges TEETH I'D into ITETHED; 'raid' is the slang sense of a police swoop.
explanation.definitionFit: To bite the dust is an idiom for failing or being destroyed.

clue.text: Essay ain't bad to start with? The opposite

indicators.note: to start with says the shuffled letters come at the front
bad means wrong, so these letters are rearranged

parts.note: a thesis is a long essay or dissertation

explanation.surface: An essay that isn't poor from the outset is the reverse of expectations.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bad' signals the rearrangement of AIN'T (giving ANTI), and 'to start with' puts it at the front rather than describing the essay's opening.
explanation.definitionFit: An antithesis is the direct contrary of something, its exact reverse.

clue.text: Somewhere near a stadium, German disappears

indicators.note: disappears says the letter for German leaves the word for stadium

parts.note: a ground is a sports stadium

explanation.surface: Somewhere close to a sports arena, a German player has vanished.
explanation.definitionFit: Around can mean approximately in the vicinity, as in 'he's around somewhere'.

clue.text: Fine writer always entertains officer

parts.note: a pen is a writing implement

indicators.note: to entertain a guest is to take them in, so the word for always holds the officer

parts.note: ay (or aye) is an old word for always
LT is the abbreviation for lieutenant, an officer

explanation.surface: A good author is always hosting a military officer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Fine' looks like an adjective praising the writer; it is the noun, a fine imposed as punishment.
explanation.definitionFit: A penalty is a punishment such as a fine paid for breaking a rule.

clue.text: Poisonous plant US city vagrant keeps in vase

parts.note: LA is Los Angeles

indicators.note: keeps in means holds inside, so the tramp holds the vase

parts.note: a bum is a US term for a tramp or vagrant
an urn is a vase

explanation.surface: A homeless person in an American city keeps a toxic plant in a pot.
explanation.definitionFit: Laburnum is a tree with yellow flowers whose seeds are highly toxic.

clue.text: Cruelly dry year restricts everything

indicators.note: restricts means confines, so the outer pieces confine the word for everything

parts.note: brut describes very dry champagne
all means everything

explanation.surface: A harsh drought year limits everything.
explanation.definitionFit: Brutally means in a savage, cruel manner.

clue.text: Fool breaks ring finger

indicators.note: breaks means cuts into, so the word for fool splits the word for ring

parts.note: to dial is to ring someone on the phone
a git is British slang for a stupid or contemptible person

explanation.surface: An idiot fractures a ring finger.
explanation.walkthrough: 'ring finger' reads as one phrase; 'ring' is DIAL and 'finger' is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Digital is an adjective meaning of the fingers, and also, as a noun, a finger itself.

clue.text: They're regularly seen after returning to Jack's pad

indicators.note: after places the picked letters behind the turned-round word

parts.note: J is the abbreviation for jack in a pack of cards

indicators.note: returning means going back, so the little word to is read right to left
regularly means taking every other letter of the word they're

explanation.surface: A cryptic remark about people regularly spotted once they've gone back to Jack's flat.
explanation.walkthrough: 'pad' suggests a flat; here it is a notepad.
explanation.definitionFit: A jotter is a small notebook or notepad for quick notes.

clue.text: Cheesemakers use this apple

definitions.meaning: the curdling agent from calves' stomachs used to set milk for cheese
an old dessert apple variety, also spelt reinette

explanation.definitionFit: One sense is the enzyme that curdles milk; the other is a variety of eating apple.

clue.text: Brainbox has audible row

indicators.note: audible says the word for row is spoken, giving a word that sounds the same

parts.note: to scull is to row with oars

explanation.surface: A clever person is having a noisy argument.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Brainbox' suggests a clever person; it is the box holding the brain. 'row' looks like a quarrel.
explanation.definitionFit: The skull is the bony case that holds the brain, a literal brain box.

clue.text: Disaster as dons take her dancing

indicators.note: to don is to put on, so the shuffled letters wrap themselves round the word for as
dancing means moving about, so the letters of take her are rearranged

parts.note: qua is a Latin-derived word meaning 'in the capacity of', that is, as

explanation.surface: University fellows taking a woman dancing turns into a catastrophe.
explanation.walkthrough: 'dons' looks like Oxford tutors; it is the verb, putting on, so the anagram of TAKE HER (EARTHKE) wraps QUA.
explanation.definitionFit: An earthquake is a natural catastrophe, a classic example of a disaster.

clue.text: Relish taking part in quizzes, typically

indicators.note: taking part in says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: Someone loves taking part in pub quizzes, as people generally do.
explanation.definitionFit: Zest is keen enjoyment or gusto, a synonym of relish as a noun.

clue.text: With head lowered, stab monster

indicators.note: in a down clue, the head is the top letter, and lowering it moves it further down the word

parts.note: to gore is to pierce with horns, to stab

explanation.surface: A bull charging head down to gore a monster.
explanation.definitionFit: An ogre is a man-eating giant of folklore, a kind of monster.

clue.text: News about one different composer

indicators.note: about means surrounding, so the two letters go round the rest

parts.note: N is the abbreviation for new, so 'news' is read as two of them
one is the Roman numeral I
else means other or different

explanation.surface: A report about a different composer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'News' is read as the plural of N (new), giving N and N to wrap the rest.
explanation.definitionFit: Carl Nielsen was a Danish composer famous for his six symphonies.

clue.text: Be wrong about mounting resistance

indicators.note: in a down clue, mounting means going upwards, so the word for about is read bottom to top

parts.note: re means about or concerning
R is the physics symbol for resistance

explanation.surface: Making a mistake about growing opposition.
explanation.definitionFit: To err is to make a mistake, a direct synonym.

clue.text: English doctor cracks quiet joke

indicators.note: cracks means breaks into, so these letters split the word for quiet

parts.note: a lull is a quiet spell
a GP is a general practitioner, a family doctor

explanation.surface: An English doctor breaks a calm silence with a gag.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cracks' suggests cracking a joke; it is the containment signal, breaking into the word for quiet.
explanation.definitionFit: A leg-pull is a hoax or tease played on someone, a kind of joke.

clue.text: Old timer's rambling anecdote ultimately is boring

indicators.note: rambling means wandering about, so these letters are mixed up
ultimately points to the final letter of the word anecdote

explanation.surface: A veteran's long-winded story is, in the end, tedious.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Old timer' looks like one phrase; 'Old' gives O to be mixed with TIMERS.
explanation.definitionFit: Tiresome means tedious or wearying, the same as boring.

clue.text: Holy person occupies most room in church

indicators.note: occupies means sits inside, so the saint goes within the word for most

parts.note: very can mean most, as in 'the very best'
ST is the abbreviation for saint

explanation.surface: A saintly figure takes up most of the space in a church.
explanation.definitionFit: A vestry is the room in a church where vestments are kept and clergy robe.
